newsitem.title: KENYA: Uganda denies sending troops into Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Uganda denies sending troops into Zaire.

text.p: Uganda on Wednesday denied it had sent several thousand troops into eastern Zaire, where rebels are fighting the country's army, terming latest Zairean allegations false.

"It is absolute falsehood. It is in fact laughable that we would be so stupid as to openly send troops into Zaire. Even the geographical locations mentioned do not make sense," Hope Kivengere, spokeswoman for President Yoweri Museveni, told Reuters by telephone from Kampala.

Zaire has repeatedly accused Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of backing rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), led by veteran opposition politician Laurent Kabila.

On Wednesday, Zaire's military high command said in a statement that several thousand Ugandans had invaded its territory, with some units heading towards the jungle city of Kisangani and mineral-rich Shaba province.

The statement by Zaire's military high command said about 2,000 Ugandan troops who left Fizi, some 100 km (60 miles) south of the rebel-held eastern Zaire town of Uvira, were heading in direction of Kalemie in Shaba Province.
